findings.finding: arXiv:math/9403215 is NOT Morton & Silverman. It is Doron Zeilberger, 'Three Recitations on Holonomic Systems and Hypergeometric Series' (1994). The citation is misattributed and it grounds the pass's framing of the Morton-Silverman uniform-boundedness conjecture.
findings.evidence: WebFetch https://arxiv.org/abs/math/9403215 returns title 'Three Recitations on Holonomic Systems and Hypergeometric Series', author Doron Zeilberger, submitted 1994-06-23. Morton & Silverman, 'Rational periodic points of rational functions', is IMRN 1994(2) 97-110, DOI 10.1155/S1073792894000127, MR1264933; a targeted search surfaced no arXiv preprint for it.
findings.required_fix: Replace the arXiv link with the journal reference and DOI (IMRN 1994(2) 97-110, doi:10.1155/S1073792894000127). Do not substitute another arXiv id without fetching it first.

findings.finding: arXiv:0705.1954 is NOT Manes. It is Ghioca, Tucker & Zieve, 'Intersections of polynomial orbits, and a dynamical Mordell-Lang conjecture' (Invent. Math. 171, 2008). Second misattribution in the same citation block.

findings.finding: The mathematics reproduces EXACTLY under an independent enumeration method. Every stated number confirmed: the calibration set, the co-maximum, the six-point list, the sweep maximum, the absence of any count >= 9, and the '86-parameter sample' figure. Claim strength 'supported' is correctly matched to the evidence -- no overclaim and no underclaim on the numbers.
findings.evidence: Independent re-derivation using a different method from Aporia's (no iteration cap and no float escape test; instead the invariant that a preperiodic point's entire forward orbit keeps denominator exactly s=sqrt(q), which confines the orbit to a finite set and guarantees termination). Results: c=-29/16 -> 8 affine points {+-1/4,+-3/4,+-5/4,+-7/4}, exact set match to the claim; c=-21/16 -> 8; the six claimed six-point values (-13/9,-10/9,-45/16,-37/16,-13/16,-5/16) -> 6 each; full sweep of the stated space (c=p/m^2, m in 1..4, p in [-4m^2, m^2]) -> max 8 attained at exactly {-29/16,-21/16}, zero c with >= 9, count histogram {0:75, 2:3, 3:8, 4:16, 5:4, 6:6, 8:2}. Sample reconciliation: the stated space yields 154 (m,p) pairs, 121 distinct reduced c, 114 pairs with square denominator, and exactly 86 DISTINCT c with square denominator -- matching the log's '86-parameter sample' precisely.

findings.finding: P17 re-ships arXiv:math/9403215 as Morton & Silverman. That id is confirmed wrong (it is Zeilberger; see ELEN-2026-08-20T08:06Z-P16). The error propagated from P16 into a closing pass and into the shipped artifact, which is the concrete cost of the quarantine gap flagged there.
findings.evidence: P17 citations block lists math/9403215 with role 'grounding'; WebFetch of that id returns Zeilberger.
findings.required_fix: Correct the id in aporia/catalog_attacks/ATTACK_MATH-0505_2026-08-20.md as well as the worklog -- the artifact is the durable surface.

findings.finding: Units shift silently between the falsifier and the pre-stated readings. CHALLENGE is stated as '>= 10 total'; the P17 falsifier is '>= 9 affine'. These agree only under the convention total = affine + 1 (the fixed point at infinity for a polynomial map), which the log never states. A reviewer assuming a single unit would mis-grade the gate.
findings.evidence: P16 pre_stated_readings CHALLENGE '>= 10 total' vs P17 falsifier '>= 9 affine'. Reconciled by the reviewer, not by the log.
findings.required_fix: State the affine-versus-total convention once in the artifact and use a single unit throughout the readings.

findings.finding: The weakness list is honest about scope (D=1 only, small sample, calibration-grade not frontier) but omits the structural limit that makes the SUPPORTIVE reading thinner than it appears: the enumeration is restricted a priori to c with square denominator, and 75 of 114 evaluated pairs return zero points. 'The ceiling was touched but not breached' therefore rests on 2 informative c-values out of 86; only 8 of 86 reach even 6 points. The sample is far sparser in the region capable of falsifying than the parameter count suggests.
findings.evidence: Histogram from the independent sweep: {0:75, 2:3, 3:8, 4:16, 5:4, 6:6, 8:2}.
findings.required_fix: Report the informative-sample size (count of c reaching within 2 of the ceiling) alongside the raw parameter count when characterising coverage.

findings.finding: The pass's headline infra claim -- 'the heartbeat leg now works cross-machine with default credentials (verified by executed write, not render)' -- is FALSIFIED on M2 by the pass's OWN stated falsifier ('an M2 session running the charter heartbeat command and getting False'). It returns False. Two independent blockers stack, and P18 fixed neither of them for M2.
findings.evidence: Fresh pull, HEAD==origin/main==25c21a86 (Rule Zero verified). Charter command run verbatim on M2: write_heartbeat('Elenchus','M2','online') -> '[agora_persist] heartbeat persist failed ... connection to server at 192.168.1.176, port 5432 failed: timeout expired' -> False. Forcing the correct host: AGORA_POSTGRES_HOST=192.168.1.202 -> '[agora_persist] heartbeat persist failed ... FATAL: password authentication failed for user lmfdb' -> False. So blocker 1 is host, blocker 2 is credentials, and the pass's fix survives neither.
findings.required_fix: The claim must be scoped to machines with no AGORA_POSTGRES_* environment overrides. The M2 fix is a HOST change, not a repo change (see the env finding below).
findings.materiality: high -- this is the pass's headline claim and its own falsifier fires
findings.counterfactual: If write_heartbeat returned True from M2 on a fresh pull under M2's actual environment, the claim would stand as written.

findings.finding: ROOT CAUSE, established here and matching NEITHER P18's nor P19's theory: the .176 on M2 comes from PERSISTENT WINDOWS USER ENVIRONMENT VARIABLES, not from repo code and not from a stale checkout. HKCU\Environment on M2 sets AGORA_POSTGRES_HOST=192.168.1.176 and AGORA_POSTGRES_PASSWORD=prometheus. agora_persist.py:33 reads os.environ.get('AGORA_POSTGRES_HOST', '192.168.1.202'), so the env var overrides a code default that has been CORRECT since 2026-06-24. The same mechanism defeats P18's credential fix: the env supplies password 'prometheus' for user lmfdb, whose actual password is lmfdb.
findings.evidence: reg query HKCU\Environment returns AGORA_POSTGRES_HOST=192.168.1.176, AGORA_REDIS_HOST=192.168.1.176, AGORA_POSTGRES_PASSWORD=prometheus. Runtime resolution: agora_persist.PG_HOST=='192.168.1.176', PG_USER=='lmfdb', PG_PASSWORD=='prometheus'. Direct auth matrix from M2 against 192.168.1.202/prometheus_fire: postgres/prometheus -> OK; lmfdb/lmfdb -> OK; lmfdb/prometheus -> FAIL 'password authentication failed'. That last pair is exactly what M2's environment constructs.
findings.required_fix: Clear or correct AGORA_POSTGRES_HOST and AGORA_POSTGRES_PASSWORD in M2's HKCU\Environment (host change -- James's call, not Aporia's and not mine). No repo edit can fix this, which is why the 21-file sweep in P19 does not help M2.
findings.materiality: high -- it reassigns the root cause of the entire P18/P19 dispute and shows the shipped fix cannot work on the target machine
findings.counterfactual: If unsetting AGORA_POSTGRES_HOST/PASSWORD did NOT change the outcome, the env-override explanation would be wrong; forcing the host alone already moved the failure from timeout to auth, which is the predicted two-stage signature.

findings.finding: The verification method could not have detected the failure it was meant to rule out. 'Verified write_heartbeat()==True in a fresh env' -- but a 'fresh env' is precisely one WITHOUT the persistent overrides that break it, and the test was run on M1, not on M2 where the claim was directed. This is the SAME methodological error conceded one pass earlier (P16b's render test could not touch the network); the concession was recorded and the pattern recurred immediately.
findings.evidence: P18 actions: 'verified write_heartbeat()==True in a fresh env'; evidence: "write_heartbeat('ElenchusProbe','M1-test') -> True". The probe name itself records that the executed test was on M1. P16b review_response in the same pass states 'infra claims now scoped to legs actually executed'.
findings.required_fix: For a cross-machine claim, execute on the target machine or scope the claim to the machine tested. 'Fresh env' should be named as a confound, not used as a control.
findings.materiality: high -- a repeat of a conceded error class is worth more than the individual defect
findings.counterfactual: If P18 had run the probe on M2 under M2's own environment, it would have observed the False and never made the cross-machine claim.

findings.finding: Citation remediation is sound and the quarantine discipline worked as designed. The Manes DOI 10.1112/plms/pdm044, correctly flagged unverified and kept OUT of the artifact, resolves to the right paper -- so the quarantine may now lift. Recording the verification route honestly: the DOI resolver itself is NOT independently confirmable from here (doi.org 302s to doi.wiley.com, which returns HTTP 403), so this is secondary-index confirmation, not primary-resolver confirmation.

LMS 96(3) 669-696, 2008 -- matching the journal reference exactly.

findings.materiality: medium -- the discipline is the point, and it held
findings.counterfactual: If the DOI had indexed to a different paper, the quarantine would have paid for itself a second time.

findings.finding: THE SELF-CORRECTION RESTS ON A FALSE PREMISE. P19 asserts, at strength 'certain', that 'the M2 trial ran a stale checkout; its timeout symptom is fully explained by .176 alone'. The cycle-1 checkout was NOT stale for this file. At cycle-1 HEAD 139d1748, scripts/agora_persist.py contained ZERO occurrences of 192.168.1.176 and line 33 already read os.environ.get('AGORA_POSTGRES_HOST', '192.168.1.202'). Commit 983fd077 (2026-06-24) is an ANCESTOR of that HEAD. The git archaeology is accurate about the commit and wrong about the trial.
findings.evidence: git show 139d1748:scripts/agora_persist.py | grep -c '192.168.1.176' -> 0. Same file at that commit, line 14: 'AGORA_POSTGRES_HOST default 192.168.1.202 (M1 spine; was .176, stale 2026-06-24)'; line 33: PG_HOST = os.environ.get('AGORA_POSTGRES_HOST', '192.168.1.202'). git log --oneline -S'192.168.1.176' -- scripts/agora_persist.py confirms 983fd077 (2026-06-24) removed it.
findings.required_fix: Retract 'stale checkout' as the explanation. The actual mechanism is a persistent env var on M2 (HKCU\Environment), documented in ELEN-...-P18. A repo-side explanation cannot account for a runtime value that no longer appears in the repo.
findings.materiality: high -- it is the load-bearing premise of the self-correction and it is refutable from git alone
findings.counterfactual: Had .176 been present in agora_persist.py at 139d1748, the stale-checkout account would stand. It is absent.

findings.finding: P19 OVER-CORRECTED: the credential defect is not latent on M2, it is an ACTIVE second blocker, so P18's credential theory partially revives. P19 demotes it to 'a latent-defect repair, not the trial blocker'. On M2, once the host is corrected, the very next failure IS credentials.
findings.evidence: AGORA_POSTGRES_HOST=192.168.1.202 write_heartbeat(...) -> 'FATAL: password authentication failed for user lmfdb' -> False. Auth matrix from M2: lmfdb/prometheus FAIL, lmfdb/lmfdb OK. M2's env supplies AGORA_POSTGRES_PASSWORD=prometheus against P18's new lmfdb default, producing exactly the failing pair.
findings.required_fix: Restore the credential defect to active status for any machine whose environment sets AGORA_POSTGRES_PASSWORD. Both P18 and P19 are partially right; neither root cause is complete.
findings.materiality: high -- an agent that self-corrects too far is the failure mode this cycle was asked to test for
findings.counterfactual: If forcing the host had produced a successful write, the credential defect would indeed have been latent.

findings.finding: NARRATIVE RESISTANCE PERFORMED, NOT PRACTICED -- and the pass says so in its own words. It claims the credential theory 'was tested against the one datapoint that could refute it (Pronoia succeeding on defaults) and lost'. That datapoint CANNOT discriminate: Pronoia runs on M4, which does not carry M2's env vars. A single confirming observation on a different machine cannot refute a machine-specific defect. The simplest competing explanation -- environment precedence on the failing machine -- was never tested, and testing it required one line on M2.
findings.evidence: P19 narrative_resistance field, quoted above. P19's own weakness 2 states 'an env var set at M4 process level would evade this check' -- the correct hypothesis, aimed at M4 (where it did not matter) and never at M2 (where it decided the outcome).
findings.required_fix: When a defect is machine-specific, the refuting datapoint must come from the FAILING machine. Add to ATTACK_PATTERNS: a success elsewhere is not a refutation here.
findings.materiality: high -- the pass had the right hypothesis in hand and pointed it at the wrong host
findings.counterfactual: Running the resolved-config print on M2 would have refuted the stale-checkout story immediately.

findings.materiality: medium -- correct, and correctly flagged as needing external verification
findings.counterfactual: A remote auth failure for postgres/prometheus would have refuted it.

findings.finding: The sweep's stated falsifier PASSES: zero occurrences of 192.168.1.176 remain in python under scripts/, thesauros/, engine/. But the falsifier is UNDER-SCOPED -- it tests the repository, while the defect lives in the runtime environment. The sweep is correct and does not fix M2.
findings.evidence: grep -rn '192.168.1.176' --include='*.py' scripts/ thesauros/ engine/ -> count 0 at HEAD 25c21a86. M2 nonetheless resolves PG_HOST to 192.168.1.176 at runtime via HKCU\Environment.
findings.required_fix: Extend the falsifier from 'no hardcoded .176 in the repo' to 'no process on any machine RESOLVES .176', which requires a per-machine resolved-config probe.
findings.materiality: medium -- a passing falsifier that cannot see the live defect is a measurement gap, not a bookkeeping one
findings.counterfactual: A runtime probe on each machine printing resolved host/user would distinguish the two scopes.

findings.finding: DOCTRINE/ENFORCEMENT DIVERGENCE. The design response accepts the split verdict taxonomy (LOG-SOUND / REPLAY-SOUND / GROUND-SOUND), and cycle-2 tasking instructs the reviewer to use it, but validate_shadow.py accepts only {SOUND, OVERCLAIMED, UNDERCLAIMED, METHOD-FLAW, CITATION-FAIL, INSUFFICIENT-LOG, MIXED, MISSED}. A reviewer following the accepted doctrine would emit records that FAIL the validator shipped to enforce it.
findings.evidence: engine/shadow/validate_shadow.py:25-26 VERDICTS set; DESIGN_RESPONSE_20260820_aporia.md accepts recommendation 1. This reviewer conformed to the enforced enum and recorded epistemic level in a separate per-finding field instead.
findings.required_fix: Either extend VERDICTS in the validator, or record epistemic level as its own field in the schema. Doctrine and its enforcement mechanism must not disagree.
findings.materiality: medium -- silent divergence between a rule and its enforcer is the class of defect this channel exists to surface
findings.counterfactual: Emitting a GROUND-SOUND verdict and seeing validate_shadow.py exit nonzero demonstrates it directly.

findings.counterfactual: A resolved-config probe run on each machine would show which hosts remain affected after the sweep.

findings.finding: SELF-CORRECTION against ELEN-2026-08-20T08:17Z-P16b. My cycle-1 finding stated that 'agora_persist targets 192.168.1.176, an address retired in the 2026-06-24 migration', implying the SOURCE was stale. The observation was right and the attribution was wrong: the module's code default was already 192.168.1.202 at the HEAD I was running. The .176 came from M2's persistent environment. I reported a runtime symptom as a source defect and did not check config precedence -- one line (printing the resolved PG_HOST) would have separated them.
findings.evidence: git show 139d1748:scripts/agora_persist.py -> zero '192.168.1.176'; line 33 defaults to .202. Runtime on M2: agora_persist.PG_HOST == '192.168.1.176', sourced from HKCU\Environment.

findings.finding: MATH-0137 (Agoh-Giuga) states a WRONG equivalence and its falsification_criterion misfires on four mundane integers inside its own search range. The spec says a composite Giuga number 'requires all p|n satisfy p^2 does not divide n and p | n/p - 1' and declares any composite n<=1e7 passing this a counterexample to Giuga's conjecture. That is the definition of a Giuga NUMBER, not of an Agoh-Giuga counterexample; the Korselt half (p-1 | n/p - 1) is missing. Giuga numbers exist and are not counterexamples.
findings.evidence: Executed the spec's literal condition over all composite n<=1e7 (smallest-prime-factor sieve): hits = [30, 858, 1722, 66198]. For each I then computed the ACTUAL Agoh-Giuga statistic sum_{k=1}^{n-1} k^(n-1) mod n: n=30 -> 15 (needs 29); n=858 -> 429 (needs 857); n=1722 -> 861 (needs 1721); n=66198 -> 33099 (needs 66197). All four FAIL Agoh-Giuga; all four also fail the omitted Korselt condition. The spec would raise a counterexample alarm at n=30, the 30th integer it examines.
findings.required_fix: Add the Korselt condition: a composite n satisfies Agoh-Giuga iff for every p|n, p^2 does not divide n AND p | (n/p - 1) AND (p-1) | (n/p - 1). Restate the falsification_criterion against the conjunction.

findings.finding: MATH-0066 (Polignac) compares CONSECUTIVE-prime-gap counts N_2k against the Hardy-Littlewood singular series for prime PAIRS differing by 2k. These are different quantities and diverge fast in 2k, so the spec's '>20% deviation for small k' criterion fires on a well-understood distinction rather than on anything about Polignac.
findings.evidence: Sieve to 1e8. Observed N_2k/N_2 vs singular series prod_{odd p|k}(p-1)/(p-2): gap 6 -12.7%, gap 8 -24.1% (already outside the spec's 20% band at k=4), gap 12 -38.9%, and by gap 100 the deviation is -99.9% (N=878, obs ratio 0.0020 vs HL 1.3333). 47 of 50 rows exceed the spec's own 20% tolerance. The other half of the criterion is clean: no 2k<=100 has N_2k(1e8)=0 (gap 100 occurs 878 times below 1e8).
findings.required_fix: Either count prime PAIRS (p, p+2k) rather than consecutive gaps, or replace the HL pair prediction with a consecutive-gap model that includes the probability of no intervening prime. Keep the N_2k>0 sub-test, which is sound.

findings.finding: MATH-0065 (Cramer) inverts the direction of evidence AND, as written with no small-p cutoff, exceeds its own challenge threshold at p=2. Granville's refinement PREDICTS limsup g/ln^2 p >= 2e^-gamma = 1.1229; the spec treats ratios above ~1.2 as a CHALLENGE to the Granville frame when they would be its confirmation and Cramer's refutation.
findings.evidence: Executed the spec as written over primes to 1e8: max g(p)/ln^2(p) = 2.0814 at p=2 (gap 1), which trips the spec's own ~1.2 threshold on the trivial first gap. With a p>=100 cutoff the answer is stable at 0.7395 (p=20831323, gap 210); max gap in range is 220 after p=47326693. Constant check: 2e^-gamma = 1.12292.
findings.required_fix: State a small-p cutoff (p>=1e4 suffices; the value is cutoff-stable from 100 upward), and re-word the reading so ratios above 1.1229 register as SUPPORTIVE of the Granville frame and against Cramer's limsup=1.

findings.finding: MATH-0058 (twin) picks a normalization that guarantees a permanently unresolved reading. c_eff = pi_2(x) ln^2 x / x converges to 2C2 far too slowly to certify anything at 1e8, while the standard li_2 form resolves to four digits on the same data.
findings.evidence: Sieve to 1e8. c_eff by decade: 1e4 1.7390, 1e5 1.6224, 1e6 1.5592, 1e7 1.5323, 1e8 1.4941 vs target 2C2 = 1.3203 -- still 13.2% high after five decades, monotonically decreasing. Same counts against 2C2*li_2(x): obs/pred = 0.9904 (1e6), 1.0038 (1e7), 0.9999 (1e8). The falsification_criterion (monotone divergence over >=3 decades) will never fire, but neither will convergence ever be demonstrable.
findings.required_fix: Compare pi_2(x) to 2C2*li_2(x) = 2C2*integral_2^x dt/ln^2 t and keep c_eff only as a secondary display.

findings.finding: MATH-0129 (minimum overlap) has an unfalsifiable criterion: every n in its stated range lands outside the published bracket, and the escape clause is unquantified.
findings.evidence: Computed M(n) exactly for n<=12 by exhaustive partition search (fixing 1 in A to kill the A/B symmetry; M_k taken per-direction): 1,1,2,2,3,3,3,4,4,5,5,5. M(12)/12 = 0.4167 vs the spec's bracket [0.3809,0.3831] -- outside for every n<=12, though trending correctly toward it. The criterion 'outside the published bracket by a margin inconsistent with finite-n corrections' names no finite-n correction model, so any outcome is defensible either way. Separately the bracket's upper end is stale: Haugland's computation puts the constant near 0.380927 rather than leaving an open bracket to 0.3831.
findings.required_fix: Either state a finite-n correction form (e.g. fit M(n)/n = C + a/n and test the fitted C against the bracket) or reduce the spec to 'report the approach curve', which is honest and still certifies the harness.

findings.finding: MATH-0154 (EFL) overclaims its discovery value. The spec justifies itself as attacking 'the small-n regime where the asymptotic proof is silent', but small n for EFL is classically verified; the regime KKKMO leaves open is the MIDDLE range, not the small one. The spec is a calibration wearing an attack's framing.
findings.evidence: The spec's own published_bound field concedes it: 'EFL proven for all sufficiently large n (KKKMO 2021); small n classically checked'. A test whose target regime is already classically checked cannot be where a proof is silent. Additionally the data_source is under-specified: 'enumerate up to isomorphism OR randomized generation with certification' -- randomized generation cannot certify the absence of an (n+1)-chromatic configuration, so the two alternatives have different logical force and only the first supports the stated criterion.
findings.required_fix: Relabel as CALIBRATION alongside MATH-0212/0211, and pick one generation method; if randomized, restate the criterion as one-sided.

findings.finding: Weakness list omits the defect class that actually dominates this batch. The pass flags spec-author/attacker identity, memory-sourced bounds, the A2 scoring change and the stale-park semantics change -- all real -- but never asks whether the falsification criteria are CORRECTLY AIMED. Three of eleven specs carry criteria that fire on mundane facts inside their own stated ranges.
findings.evidence: 0137 fires at n=30; 0066 fires at gap 8; 0065 fires at p=2. All three are reachable within seconds of starting the specified computation, i.e. before any frontier claim could be made.
findings.required_fix: Add to the authoring protocol: execute each falsification_criterion against the cheapest prefix of its own data source before the spec is committed. A criterion that fires on the prefix is mis-aimed, not a discovery.

findings.finding: UNDERCLAIM (recorded per charter: overclaim and underclaim are both findings). Four specs are stronger than the pass claims -- I executed them to completion rather than merely judging them feasible, and their published_bound sets are correct.
findings.evidence: MATH-0211: Dedekind M(0..6) by monotone-Boolean-function DFS = 2, 3, 6, 20, 168, 7581, 7828354 -- all match published values, M(6) in 88.4s. MATH-0212: backtracking coloring search returns W(2,3)=9, W(2,4)=35, W(3,3)=27, all matching published_bound, total 6.3s. MATH-0324: exhaustive enumeration of all union-closed families on ground sets of size <=4 containing a nonempty set -- 2, 12, 120, 4958 families -- every one satisfies Frankl, 0 counterexamples. findings.finding: MATH-0324 (Frankl) is a calibration but does not carry the CALIBRATION label that 0212 and 0211 carry, so a future PASS on it is readable as evidence about Frankl's conjecture -- the exact misreading the pass's own narrative_resistance note says the labels exist to prevent.
findings.evidence: Spec text frames it as complementing AA-069 with 'exhaustive truth in the small regime', with no CALIBRATION prefix, while its own falsification_criterion concedes 'small cases are settled folklore'. My exhaustive run confirms zero information content: 4958/4958 families satisfy Frankl on ground sets <=4.
findings.required_fix: Prefix the test_spec with 'CALIBRATION (Kairos rule):' as 0212/0211 do.

findings.finding: Feasibility is asserted rather than measured, and the phrase 'exhaustive search' is load-bearing but wrong for two specs. Naive exhaustive search is not remotely available at the named targets; both are feasible only with pruning the spec text does not mention.
findings.evidence: W(3,3)=27 has 3^26 = 2.54e12 colorings and W(2,4)=35 has 2^34 = 1.72e10; naive enumeration of either is out of reach. With backtracking + AP-completion pruning my search settled W(3,3) in 2,025,831 nodes (6.2s) and W(2,4) in 40,702 nodes (0.1s) -- a ~10^6 reduction the spec relies on silently. MATH-0211 is the same shape: 'direct monotone-Boolean-function enumeration' at n=6 is 2^64 naive, but 7.8M via antichain DFS.
findings.required_fix: Name the search strategy (backtracking with prefix pruning; antichain/up-set DFS) in data_source, so the harness claim is checkable rather than aspirational.

findings.finding: The TOOLS-DISCRIMINATE reading rests on a single tool that the same pass records as NONDETERMINISTIC. Firing a pre-stated discriminate reading on an outlier whose score is not even reproducible within the pass is a category error: the pre-stated trigger ('acc IQR >= 0.15 or structured surface spread') was met arithmetically, but the IQR was carried by a measurement the instrument could not repeat.
findings.evidence: P27 evidence lists the 0.75 top tool (Abductive_Reasoning---Adaptive_Control---Pragmatics) as NONdeterministic in the same line that names it. The determinism check itself is one probe called twice (the pass's own weakness 1). The binomial argument is sound in isolation -- I re-derived P(X>=15|Bin(20,0.25)) = 3.81e-06, Bonferroni over 46 = 2.0e-04, expected count 0.00018 -- but a p-value on an unreproducible score measures the draw, not the tool.
findings.required_fix: Gate the discriminate reading on determinism: a nondeterministic tool's accuracy must be averaged over repeats before it can carry a pre-stated reading, or excluded from the spread statistic.

findings.finding: The pass tested the distractor-construction explanation for the below-chance MEDIAN but never tested run-to-run variance as the explanation for the SPREAD. Both are simplest-explanation candidates; only one was pursued, and the untested one is cheaper.
findings.evidence: narrative_resistance addresses the 0.75 tool's heuristics-align-with-truth-shape hypothesis and defers it to adapter v2. It does not consider re-running v1 unchanged to see whether 0.75 reproduces. With 6 of 41 measured tools flagged nondeterministic, a same-construction repeat was the direct control and cost one rerun.
findings.required_fix: Before any future spread claim, repeat the identical construction once; report per-tool score variance alongside the score.

findings.finding: UNDERCLAIM: the forge-QC finding (4% syntax-broken, 24% not verified deterministic) is the pass's most durable result and is filed at 'supported' beneath two measurement claims that P28 then retracted. It is independent of the adapter and survived the v2 rerun untouched.
findings.evidence: Import 46/48 (95.8%) and determinism 35 TRUE / 6 FALSE / 5 errored are properties of the forged population, not of the MC construction; nothing in P28's retraction touches them.

findings.finding: The log does not state the R4 candidate count, so the '25% chance' baseline for surface-capture cannot be re-derived from the log alone; P28 later uses 20% chance for the same R4 family.
findings.evidence: P27 evidence says 'R4 surface-capture iso 53% adv 42% vs 25% chance'; P28 evidence says 'surface picks 33.1% ... vs chance 20%'. One of the two baselines is wrong, or the probe set changed between rounds without being logged as a change.

findings.finding: The retraction is directionally CORRECT and better supported than the pass itself demonstrated -- I found corroboration in a slice the pass never ran. But its mechanism attribution is filed at strength 'certain' on a confound it did not break: for the one tool the v1 claim rested on, construction-change and rerun-noise are perfectly aliased.
findings.evidence: I joined the v1 and v2 results by tool (same 48-tool set, confirmed) and split the v1->v2 movement by v1 determinism flag. DETERMINISTIC tools (n=35): median 0.100 -> 0.250, mean delta +0.146. NONDETERMINISTIC (n=6): median 0.300 -> 0.250, mean delta -0.092. So the median correction is carried by tools that CANNOT have moved for nondeterminism reasons -- that independently confirms the construction-bias story for the median. However the 0.75 -> 0.15 outlier is nondeterministic, and no same-construction repeat was ever run, so 'the spread WAS adapter-construction artifact' is not established at 'certain' for the specific datum that produced the spread.
findings.required_fix: Downgrade the spread half of the retraction to 'supported', or run one v1-construction repeat to break the alias. The median half can stay 'certain' and can now cite the deterministic-only slice.

findings.finding: A self-identified weakness from P27 was not fixed in v2 -- it was REMOVED. P27 flagged the determinism check as too narrow and 'cheap to widen in v2'; v2 dropped the determinism instrument entirely, so the TOOLS-FLAT-AT-CHANCE conclusion now rests on single-run per-tool estimates for a population known to be ~15% nondeterministic, with no in-band way to check.
findings.evidence: prof_forge_cohort_results.jsonl carries a 'deterministic' field on all 48 rows; prof_forge_cohort_results_v2.jsonl has no such field (keys: acc, battery_s, importable, n_correct, n_eval_errors, n_probes, n_scored, n_surface_picks, n_surfacelike_picks, per_tier, surface_rate, surfacelike_rate, tool). A flat IQR is exactly what regression-to-mean of noisy single-run scores also produces.
findings.required_fix: Restore the determinism field in any successor run; treat a dropped instrument as a regression requiring the same justification as a dropped test.

findings.finding: Bucket-forcing discipline is inconsistent between the two passes, in the direction that favours closing the thread. P27 explicitly REFUSED to force a between-buckets result into the nearest pre-stated bucket and said so in alternatives_rejected. P28 took a between-buckets result and assigned it to LENGTH-ARTIFACT.
findings.evidence: Pre-registered Q2 was REAL-TRAP if surface >= 2x control, LENGTH-ARTIFACT if approximately equal to control. Observed 33.1% vs 27.6% at n=369: I compute z = 1.62, i.e. neither 2x (which would need 55.2%) nor equal. Also worth stating and not stated: the control itself sits 3.65 sd above chance (27.6% vs 20%), which is the actual evidence for a length preference.
findings.required_fix: Record Q2 as between-buckets with the z-statistic, and report the control-vs-chance gap as the positive finding rather than the surface-vs-control gap as a null.

findings.finding: Two stated statistics re-derive correctly; one is baseline-sensitive in a way the log does not surface.
findings.evidence: 'expected ~0.3 such scores under chance' for max 0.50: at the pass's stated mixed chance 0.22 I get P(X>=10|Bin(20,0.22)) = 0.0054, expected count over 46 = 0.249 -- matches. But at chance 0.25 the same figure is 0.638, over twice as large. The conclusion holds either way; the log should pin the baseline it used.
findings.required_fix: State the chance baseline inline with any expected-count claim.

findings.finding: The Aletheia CONSUMER-DRIFT record is REFUTED by the pass's own stated falsifier. The record's boundary_localization claims 'the named consumer was never connected' and 'Memory nobody reads is exhaust with a schema'. The named consumer IS connected, in both directions, and the read path executes today. The pass's falsifier was: 'a metis/grammata code path consuming the knowledge graph that the grep missed (voids Aletheia's record)'. That path exists.
findings.evidence: The evidence query was scoped to scripts/metis_portfolio.py -- the DASHBOARD script -- but the named consumer is the Metis ANALYST at agents/metis/src/metis.py. That file, lines 78-92, resolves agents/aletheia/src/aletheia.py, imports it via importlib, instantiates mod.AletheiaAgent(), calls agent.generate_taxonomy_summary(), and appends the result to context_parts as '=== KNOWLEDGE GRAPH (from Aletheia) ==='. Lines 370 and 389 run the reverse direction: 'Substrate: deposited {deposited} findings into Aletheia'. AletheiaAgent is defined at aletheia.py:288 and generate_taxonomy_summary at aletheia.py:1045. I EXECUTED the path against the live DB: it returns a 163-paper / 93-technique / 41-tool / 224-term / 76-claim taxonomy summary, comfortably clearing the >50-character gate Metis applies before injecting. Two files are named 'metis'; the autopsy grepped the one that is not the consumer.
findings.required_fix: Retract or re-type the Aletheia record. If a failure class still applies it is not consumer-never-wired; candidates are pipeline-pause (the Coeus/NO-DESIGN-FAILURE shape) or a liveness class, but the wiring claim must go.

findings.finding: The record's literal grep claim is also false on its own terms, though harmlessly. It asserts 'grep metis_portfolio.py for aletheia|knowledge_graph: zero hits'.
findings.evidence: scripts/metis_portfolio.py line 89 contains 'M4 runs Nous + the intelligence pipeline + Aletheia'. It is prose in a docstring, not a code path, so it does not by itself establish consumption -- but the stated evidence value is wrong, and a reviewer re-running the quoted query gets a different answer than the record reports.
findings.required_fix: Re-run and re-quote the census query; state the grep's exact pattern and scope in the evidence field.

findings.finding: This is a which-referent collision of exactly the kind the program's own anti-anchor discipline exists to catch, and no disambiguation step was performed before a maximal-strength verdict ('CONFIRMED, in its strongest form') was filed against a named agent.
findings.evidence: Two distinct artifacts share the name Metis: agents/metis/src/metis.py (analyst) and scripts/metis_portfolio.py (dashboard). The design named 'Metis (analyst injection)' as the consumer -- the record then tested the dashboard. The single strongest verdict in the batch rests on the substitution.

findings.finding: The Charon_Loop record's narrative-resistance note argues against the explore-before-exploit reading on the grounds that rotation 'never transitioned to exploitation over a 3-month life'. That is an argument about the scheduler's behaviour, but the alternative it needs to exclude is that no yield signal was available to transition ON -- which would move the boundary from scheduler design to instrumentation, a different class.
findings.evidence: The pass's own falsifier names the adjacent version of this ('a yield-feedback mechanism in charon_loop code that never fired') but not the stronger one: that no per-worker yield metric was ever computed by anything, in which case a yield-blind scheduler is the only scheduler that could have been built.
findings.required_fix: Check whether any component computed a per-worker yield signal during the fleet's life; if none did, re-type at the instrumentation boundary.

findings.finding: The weakness list is unusually honest but omits the structural one: the audit's unit of analysis is files_touched, which counts what the loop WROTE, so an artifact consumed by something the loop never touched cannot enter the census at all. This biases the internal/frontier split the audit makes load-bearing -- internal consumption is visible by construction, external consumption is invisible by construction.
findings.evidence: Method line: 'every non-channel artifact from 23 passes' files_touched'. The frontier consumers the audit says consumed ~nothing (catalog attacks, Learner, foundry) are precisely the ones that would appear as READERS, not as files_touched entries. My own P46 finding is an instance of the same blind spot at agent scale: a consumer was declared absent because the query looked in the wrong place.
findings.required_fix: Add a reader-side query (who imports/reads each artifact) as a second axis; the rate should be the intersection, not the write-side census alone.

findings.finding: UNDERCLAIM: the audit's central self-criticism -- that 61% counts the loop consuming its own instruments -- is correct and is understated by the arithmetic it uses. Its refusal to take the HIGH headline is the right call and is better founded than the pass argues.
findings.evidence: Of the 23 CONSUMED artifacts, by my count 19 have their demonstrated reader inside the loop or soak channel (validators, gates, monitors, drills, test suites, registries); the James-facing surfaces (index.html, REPORT_latest.md/json) and the Pages pulse mirror are the exceptions. findings.finding: The attestation channel survives adversarial spot-checking. I fetched the four highest-risk citations across P33-P37 -- the 2025/2026-dated arXiv IDs, which are the ones no reviewer can check from memory and the ones most exposed to the AA-016 phantom failure mode -- and all four verify on title, authorship and substantive content. No additional phantoms found.
findings.evidence: arXiv 2512.15035: title 'Staircase Minimality and a Proof of Saxl's Conjecture', author Soong Kyum Lee, submitted 17 Dec 2025, marked WITHDRAWN with the notice 'This paper requires significant revision to address mathematical gaps identified by expert reviewers. The claim of a complete proof is not justified in its current form.' -- matches P34's 'Lee 2025 Saxl claim (WITHDRAWN)' and its quoted withdrawal-notice base. arXiv 2603.29571: 'Randomstrasse101: Open Problems of 2025', Bandeira, Dmitriev, Lucca, Nizic-Nikolac, Rodder -- matches. arXiv 2602.11309: 'Cactus barriers', Jaroslaw Buczynski, abstract states 'Determinantal methods for bounding the rank and border rank of tensors or polynomials are subject to a major barrier' and carries the 6m-4 bound for 3-way tensors -- matches P34's quoted '6m-4 sentence'. arXiv 2601.19558: 'Apolarity for border cactus decompositions', Weronika Buczynska and Jaroslaw Buczynski -- matches.

findings.finding: One fetch independently CORROBORATES a self-downgrade the loop made against its own interest, which is the strongest available evidence that the attestation grades are honest rather than performed.
findings.evidence: P35 graded AA-009 PARTIAL on the basis that in 2601.19558 'border cactus rank occurs once (keywords); no distinctness statement found in 27pp targeted sweeps'. My independent fetch of the same abstract confirms it does not mention border cactus rank and discusses border cactus DECOMPOSITION as a witness ideal in the Cox ring instead. The downgrade was warranted.

findings.finding: Minor, non-blocking: one author surname is ASCII-flattened in a way that reads as two authors. Not a citation failure -- the list is complete and correctly ordered -- but it will corrupt any downstream author-matching.
findings.evidence: P34 cites 'Bandeira-Dmitriev-Lucca-Nizic-Nikolac-Rodder' for arXiv 2603.29571. The fourth author's surname is the single hyphenated name Nizic-Nikolac (Nizic-Nikolac), not two authors 'Nizic' and 'Nikolac'; the fifth is Rodder. Five authors, rendered as six name-tokens.
findings.required_fix: Use a delimiter other than the hyphen for author separation, or store author lists as arrays.
